title: Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov Max-Cut Exponent Conjecture
statement_text: For $H$ fixed and $m$ sufficiently large, every $H$-free graph $G$ with $m$ edges satisfies $\mathrm{Max\text{-}Cut}(G) \geq \frac{m}{2} + \Omega_H\!\left(m^{3/4}\right)$.
context_text: Alon, Krivelevich, and Sudakov proved that for fixed $H$ and large $m$, every $H$-free graph $G$ with $m$ edges satisfies $\mathrm{Max\text{-}Cut}(G) \geq \frac{m}{2} + m^{1/2+\varepsilon(H)}$ for some $\varepsilon(H)>0$, and conjectured the exponent $1/2$ can be replaced by $3/4$. The paper studies this in the special case $H = C_k$ for odd $k$.
paper_contribution: Theorem 1.7 proves $\mathrm{Max\text{-}Cut}(G) \geq \frac{m}{2} + \Omega_k(m^{(k+5)/(k+7)})$ for $C_k$-free graphs with odd $k \geq 3$; since $(k+5)/(k+7) > 3/4$ for all odd $k \geq 3$, this confirms the conjecture for $H = C_k$ with odd $k \geq 3$.

title: Alon et al. $C_k$-Free Max-Cut Conjecture
statement_text: For all $k \geq 3$, every $C_k$-free graph $G$ with $m$ edges satisfies $\mathrm{Max\text{-}Cut}(G) \geq \frac{m}{2} + \Omega_k\!\left(m^{(k+1)/(k+2)}\right)$.
context_text: Alon et al. conjectured this bound for all $k \geq 3$ and verified it for even $k$, showing the bound is tight for $k \in \{4, 6, 10\}$. For odd $k$, the best previously known lower bound was $\frac{m}{2} + m^{(k+1)/(k+3)+o(1)}$ due to Zeng and Hou.
paper_contribution: Theorem 1.7 proves $\mathrm{Max\text{-}Cut}(G) \geq \frac{m}{2} + \Omega_k(m^{(k+5)/(k+7)})$ for odd $k \geq 3$, improving the Zeng–Hou exponent $(k+1)/(k+3)+o(1)$ toward the conjectured exponent $(k+1)/(k+2)$.
notes: A footnote in the paper clarifies that reference [9] actually conjectured only that the bound is tight for even $k$; the full conjecture for all $k \geq 3$ as stated may be attributed differently in the literature.

title: Conjecture on sharpness of Theorem 1.1
statement_text: For each integer $r \geq 3$ there is $c_r$ such that for all positive integers $n, k$ with $n$ sufficiently large in terms of $k$, $$h(n, k, K_r) = \Theta_r\!\left(\frac{n^2}{k^{(r-1)/(r-2)}}\right),$$ i.e., the upper bound $h(n, k, K_r) \leq c_r \dfrac{n^2}{k^{(r-1)/(r-2)}}$ is tight up to the constant factor $c_r$.
context_text: For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $k$, $h(G,k)$ is the minimum number of edges whose deletion makes $G$ $k$-colourable, and $h(n,k,H)$ is the maximum of $h(G,k)$ over all $n$-vertex graphs $G$ not containing $H$ as a subgraph (the case $k=1$ is the Turán problem; Erdős's conjecture that triangle-free graphs can be made bipartite by deleting $n^2/25$ edges is the case $H=K_3$, $k=2$). The authors prove $h(n,k,K_r)\le c_r n^2/k^{(r-1)/(r-2)}$ for every $r\ge3$ and all $n,k$, and prove the matching lower bound for $r=3$. For odd cycles they determine $h(n,k,C_{2r+1})$ up to a constant factor for $n$ large, using Alon's pseudorandom graphs of large odd girth for the lower bound. A corresponding dense pseudorandom $K_r$-free construction is not known for $r\ge4$ but is conjectured to exist, and it would imply this conjecture.

title: Conjecture on sharpness of Theorem 1.5
statement_text: For each positive integer $r$, the bound $$h(n, k, W_{2r+1}) \leq c_r \frac{n^2}{k^{2 - 1/(r+1)}}$$ is tight up to the constant factor $c_r$ depending on $r$.
context_text: For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $k$, $h(G,k)$ is the minimum number of edges whose deletion makes $G$ $k$-colourable, and $h(n,k,H)$ is the maximum of $h(G,k)$ over all $n$-vertex graphs $G$ not containing $H$ as a subgraph (the case $k=1$ is the Turán problem; Erdős's conjecture that triangle-free graphs can be made bipartite by deleting $n^2/25$ edges is the case $H=K_3$, $k=2$). The wheel $W_\ell$ consists of an $\ell$-cycle plus a vertex adjacent to all its vertices. For even wheels the authors show $h(n,k,W_\ell)$ is asymptotically the same as $h(n,k,K_3)$. For odd wheels, combining their methods for cliques ($h(n,k,K_r)\le c_rn^2/k^{(r-1)/(r-2)}$) and for graphs of large odd girth ($h(n,k,C_{2r+1})=O_r(n^2/k^{r+1})$, tight for large $n$), they prove $h(n,k,W_{2r+1})\le c_rn^2/k^{2-1/(r+1)}$ for $n\ge k\ge2$, and conjecture this is tight up to the constant factor depending on $r$.

title: Question 2.1
statement_text: Given a graph $G$, how many edges of $G$ can we cover by the union of $k$ neighborhoods of vertices of $G$?
context_text: For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $k$, $u(G,k)$ is the maximum number of edges of the induced subgraph $G[N(v_1)\cup\dots\cup N(v_k)]$ over all choices of $k$ vertices $v_1,\dots,v_k$, and $m(n,k)$ is the minimum of $e(G)-u(G,k)$ over all $n$-vertex graphs $G$, i.e. the least $r$ such that in every $n$-vertex graph some $k$ neighbourhoods together induce all but at most $r$ edges. One has $m(n,1)=\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$, a strengthening of Mantel's theorem since $u(G,1)=0$ exactly when $G$ is triangle-free. Bounds on this quantity are the main tool for the authors' upper bounds on $h(n,k,H)$, the minimum number of edges whose deletion makes any $n$-vertex $H$-free graph $k$-colourable, when $H$ is a clique or an odd wheel. Via a random choice of the $k$ vertices they prove $m(n,k)\le n^2/(ek)$.

title: Open problem on $m(n,k)$ for fixed $k \geq 2$
statement_text: What is the exact or asymptotic value of $m(n,k)$ for any fixed $k \geq 2$?
context_text: For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $k$, $u(G,k)$ is the maximum number of edges of the induced subgraph $G[N(v_1)\cup\dots\cup N(v_k)]$ over all choices of $k$ vertices $v_1,\dots,v_k$, and $m(n,k)$ is the minimum of $e(G)-u(G,k)$ over all $n$-vertex graphs $G$, i.e. the least $r$ such that in every $n$-vertex graph some $k$ neighbourhoods together induce all but at most $r$ edges. One has $m(n,1)=\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$, a strengthening of Mantel's theorem since $u(G,1)=0$ exactly when $G$ is triangle-free. The authors prove $m(n,k)\le n^2/(ek)$ by choosing $k$ random vertices. An Erdős–Rényi random graph $G(n,c/k)$, with $c$ maximising $ce^{-c}-\frac c2e^{-2c}$, gives $m(n,k)\ge(1+o_k(1))(ce^{-c}-\frac c2e^{-2c})\frac{n^2}{k}$ for $n$ large in terms of $k$, which for $k$ large is within $20\%$ of the upper bound. They state that they have no idea what the exact or asymptotic value of $m(n,k)$ is for any fixed $k\ge2$.
notes: Stated as an informal open problem in the body of the paper without a labelled theorem environment.
